title: NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own) — Loss Settlement Basis and Claim Payments
content:
### How a loss is settled under NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)

Each coverage is settled separately from the latest governing adjuster report on the claim, with its own deductible.

**Building basis.** Building losses are settled at replacement cost when the tier is eligible for replacement cost settlement, the policy is designated a primary residence and the building limit is at least the lower of the tier's insurance-to-value share of the replacement cost value and the tier's statutory maximum building coverage; a manufactured home designated a primary residence that the adjuster reports as a total loss is settled at the lower of its replacement cost loss and the tier's special loss settlement multiple times its actual cash value loss; every other building loss is settled at actual cash value.

**Building payable.** The building payable is the settlement basis less the building deductible, never below zero, capped at the building limit.

**Contents.** Contents are always settled at actual cash value, the special-items part of the loss counting only up to the tier's special-items sublimit; the contents payable is that amount less the contents deductible, never below zero, capped at the contents limit.

**ICC and loss avoidance.** Increased Cost of Compliance is paid up to the tier's ICC limit without a deductible only on a community's substantial-damage determination, and loss-avoidance supplies up to the tier's loss-avoidance limit without a deductible; neither erodes the building limit.

**Successive payments.** A new payment on a coverage is the payable amount less what has already been paid net of voids on that claim and coverage (the payments issued on that claim number and coverage less the payments voided on them), and is issued only when positive. The payee is set by the mortgagee rule. A void reverses one issued payment item in full by its payment reference and never changes the payable amount; the voided amount is reissued under a new payment reference.

| Building settlement basis | When |
|---|---|
| Replacement cost | Tier eligible, primary residence, building limit at least the lower of the insurance-to-value share of replacement cost value and the statutory maximum |
| Lower of replacement cost loss and the special multiple times actual cash value loss | Manufactured home, primary residence, reported total loss |
| Actual cash value | Every other building loss |

*Hypothetical worked example.* A primary-residence policy on a replacement-cost-eligible tier has a building limit of 160,000 dollars and a stated replacement cost value of 200,000 dollars; at an 80 percent share the test figure is 160,000 dollars (lower than a 250,000-dollar maximum), so the limit meets it and the building loss is settled at replacement cost. With a replacement cost loss of 30,000 dollars and a 2,000-dollar deductible the building payable is 28,000 dollars; if 10,000 dollars has already been paid net of voids, the new payment is 18,000 dollars.
